Covered auth patterns (API keys vs. SSO service accounts), env var strategies for dev/staging/prod, example quickstarts, and next steps for a short pilot and benchmark run.
topics: Service account + KMS discussion for Private deployment
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ethan Lowe (Northforge Lead Engineer), Priya Rao (Platform Architect), Samir Patel (DevOps), Lina Gomez (Secops)

Auto-generated sections (may be imperfect):
Summary: Quick SDK walkthrough and infra handoff for multi-env integration. Discussed API key rotation, SSO, and KMS options. Agreed to pilot with 2 endpoints and run latency tests.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, im Jordan with Redwood inference, i'll kick off real quick. want to confirm agenda — walk through python + typescript sdks, auth patterns for dev/staging/prod, share quickstart scripts, and answer infra / security questions.
[00:18] Ethan (Northforge): thanks jordan. yeah our main ask is — we need a clean path to get a small pilot in staging, with predictable latency and no credential sprawl. we use github actions for ci, terraform for infra.
[00:30] Maya (Redwood SE): quick note, i'll show a sample repo and a small local mock, then how to swap to hosted vs dedicated endpoints. also cover env var patterns and short-lived service accounts.
[00:45] Priya (Northforge): and on the security side, we need KMS integration and audit logs. we have a corporate KMS and an EKM for keys. any gotchas there?
[00:58] Jordan (Redwood): good question. short answer: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS / HSM integrations; we'll share the security pack later but in practice you can configure the key ARN in the private control plane, or we can use hosted with envelope encryption. maya will go into a bit more detail.
[01:12] Maya (Redwood SE): ok jumping into code — for python it's a pip package, 'pip install redwood-inference' (note: repo name may change). sample quickstart snippet:
  
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  resp = client.generate("Summarize the incident")
  print(resp.text)

Keep the API key in your secrets manager and reference via env var in GH Actions. for typescript: 'npm i @redwood/inference' and example:
  
  import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  const out = await client.generate({ prompt: 'extract entities from text' })
  console.log(out.text)

[01:55] Samir (Northforge): quick clarif — do you recommend api keys for staging and service-accounts for prod? we want rotation and least-privilege.
[02:08] Maya (Redwood SE): yes that's the normal pattern. short-lived tokens via your identity provider (OIDC / SAML) are best for prod. On dedicated or private we can issue service principal credentials scoped to a model and route. For hosted you can use API keys with rotation stored in your secrets manager.
[02:30] Lina (Northforge): any rate limiting concerns? we might have bursts from batch jobs.
[02:38] Jordan (Redwood): Redwood has per-customer quotas; for pilot we can set a burst window and adjust. also Optimize tooling suggests batching and caching configs to reduce cost. maya will show a simple batching example.
[02:50] Maya (Redwood SE): demoing live repo now — apologies if the clip is a little choppy, the packaged script is 'scripts/quickstart_local.sh' which runs the python example and the ts example in a docker compose. key lines: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...; docker-compose up --build. for CI: use gh actions secret REDWOOD_API_KEY and the action step 'run: python examples/generate.py'
[03:20] Ethan (Northforge): could you show how to switch from hosted -> dedicated in the client? we plan to start hosted then move to dedicated capacity.
[03:28] Maya (Redwood SE): yes. in the client config you can set endpoint or model alias. example: RedwoodClient({ api_key: ..., endpoint: 'https://dedicated.eu-west.redwood.ai', model: 'gptx-8k-quant' }) — slight note, some names in the transcript might get munged, model aliasing is supported so you can keep code unchanged and just update the endpoint/model mapping in the console.
[03:55] Priya (Northforge): about envs — do you recommend different service accounts per env or shared with role scoping?
[04:02] Jordan (Redwood): recommended: unique credentials per env mapped to least-privileged roles, plus a single read-only audit key for operations. that avoids accidental cross-env calls. also use prefixing in your secrets manager (redwood/dev/, redwood/stage/, redwood/prod/).
[04:20] Samir (Northforge): will we get more detailed console screenshots?
[04:24] Jordan (Redwood): yes, we'll send the onboarding repo which includes screenshots of the Console: routes, rollout config, and the Optimize recommendations view.
[04:33] Maya (Redwood SE): switching to a short demo of Optimize suggestions — this is an auto-suggest that looks at token distributions and recommends batching sizes and quantization profile; example: if you see many short completions, decrease batch size to reduce latency, if you have lots of repeated prefixes, enable prefix caching. (audio overlap)
[04:55] Ethan (Northforge): any support for prefix/KV cache on private deployments?
[05:02] Maya (Redwood SE): yes, KV / prefix caching is supported in private/dedicated; in private you'll manage cache affinity and persistence. watch out for sequence length differences affecting kernel selection. those are performance tuning knobs we can help with.
[05:20] Priya (Northforge): sec question — audit logs retention and export. we need 12 months.
[05:27] Jordan (Redwood): we can configure audit log retention for Private; hosted tier has retention tiers, enterprise add-on for extended retention. will include details in the security doc pack.
[05:38] [10m skip in transcript for demo walkthrough]
[15:40] Maya (Redwood SE): quick demo of the sample GH Actions step:
  
  - name: Run Redwood generate
    run: python examples/generate.py
    env:
      REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}

and for typescript workflow use node and export REDWOOD_API_KEY similarly. for local testing we suggest 'direnv' or 'direnv allow' to populate envs per directory.
[16:05] Ethan (Northforge): about the quickstart repo — can you make the terraform pieces modular? we want a module to provision the networking and a module to wire in secrets to our vault.
[16:15] Maya (Redwood SE): yes, the repo includes terraform examples with a 'redwood_network' module and a 'redwood_secrets' module that shows how to put the API key in your vault and reference it in GH actions. we'll tailor that for your naming conventions.
[16:33] Lina (Northforge): for KMS we have AWS KMS with EKM, and also an HSM vendor in scope. any blockers?
[16:40] Jordan (Redwood): no blockers. private control plane supports custom KMS. there are some auth handshake steps — we will include the required role ARNs and sample terraform in the pack.
[16:52] Samir (Northforge): curious about cost controls, can we limit per-route spend?
[16:57] Maya (Redwood SE): yes, Console supports per-route quotas and alerts, plus token-based cost breakdown. also you can set automatic fallback to a cheaper model when budget thresholds are hit.
[17:12] Ethan (Northforge): what about model validation — we need to ensure outputs don't regress after quantization.
[17:18] Maya (Redwood SE): Optimize integrates with evals, you can attach a prompt set and baseline metrics; rolling quantization changes go through canary and regression alerts. we'll help set up an eval suite for your pilot.
[17:30] Jordan (Redwood): ok, a short live troubleshooting example — maya, can you run the python example and show the logs?
[17:36] Maya (Redwood SE): running now... (typing)
[17:50] Maya (Redwood SE): logs show a 401 — ok that's because the key in the container wasn't passed. i forgot to mount the secret in docker compose; fix is 'environment: - REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY}'. small things like that are common in first-run.
[18:05] Ethan (Northforge): good to know. any tips for secret rotation in GH Actions?
[18:12] Jordan (Redwood): rotate keys in your secrets manager and update the GH secret via API, or adopt OIDC federation so tokens are minted per job. OIDC avoids storing static secrets in GH.
[18:25] Priya (Northforge): OIDC would be better for us, we already use it for other cloud providers. what's required on Redwood side?
[18:31] Maya (Redwood SE): we map OIDC token claims to a Redwood role; need to configure your IdP and provide the issuer metadata. we'll share a template.
[18:45] [30m mark - deeper infra Q&A]
[30:10] Ethan (Northforge): performance wise, do you have an example JSON of throughput vs latency for a 4k sequence on your dedicated pools?
[30:20] Maya (Redwood SE): yes, we'll attach a benchmark sheet. rough numbers: p95 latency ~120ms for cached prefixes, cold-start maybe 300-500ms depending on model; throughput scales with GPU count. these are approximate; we'll run your data for an apples-to-apples.
[30:38] Samir (Northforge): for private, how do we handle outbound egress? we prefer deny-by-default.
[30:44] Jordan (Redwood): Private can run with strict egress rules; the control plane needs reachability to our management endpoints only, or air-gapped mode is possible with additional setup. we'll include the network topology doc.
[31:00] Lina (Northforge): will the console show token-level cost breakdown? operations will need that.
[31:05] Maya (Redwood SE): yes, Console exposes token and route breakdown down to request-level traces (with sampling) and cost attributions. you can also export to BigQuery or S3.
[31:20] Ethan (Northforge): ok what's the recommended pilot scope?
[31:24] Jordan (Redwood): recommended 2-week pilot: route A (customer support summarization) and Route B (entity extraction). we'll provide sample dataset and run benchmarks on both hosted and dedicated. scope includes integration, baseline runs, and an eval suite for quality checks.
[31:42] Priya (Northforge): timeline — we want to go to procurement after pilot if numbers look good. procurement requires SOC2 and ISO docs. can you provide?
[31:50] Jordan (Redwood): yes, security pack with SOC2 type II, ISO27001, third party pen test summary, and compliance contacts will be included.
[32:05] [40m mark - wrap and recap]
[40:02] Jordan (Redwood): recap: we'll share starter repo, security docs, terraform modules, and schedule the benchmark run. next meeting we'll set up a dedicated pilot channel and a Maya-led benchmarking session.
[40:15] Ethan (Northforge): great. can you also share the quickstart that shows how to switch endpoints via env var so our devs can flip from hosted to dedicated without code changes?
[40:25] Maya (Redwood SE): yes. sample env pattern: REDWOOD_ENDPOINT, REDWOOD_MODEL_ALIAS, REDWOOD_API_KEY. in code, read from env and keep defaults.
[40:38] Priya (Northforge): will you also include a template SLA for Dedicated?
[40:42] Jordan (Redwood): we will include an example SLA and notes on latency SLOs per tier.
[40:50] Samir (Northforge): any final blockers from our side? we'll need to align on network peering and CIDR.
[40:58] Jordan (Redwood): noted. action items listed earlier.
[41:10] Maya (Redwood SE): thanks everyone. i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark, and drop the repo link in the thread.
[41:20] Ethan (Northforge): thanks jordan, maya. good session.
[41:25] Meeting ended.
